prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single perfect site that does all three (beginner‑friendly plain English, shows verifiable real numbers, and openly publishes its own losses). The best approach is a small combo:

- Coin Bureau — excellent plain‑English, non‑technical crypto explainers and “how it works” guides for beginners. Good examples and walk‑throughs.
- Bankless — beginner→intermediate DeFi education in clear language, with newsletters/podcasts and practical how‑tos.
- Dune Analytics — not an “explainers” site, but it lets anyone build and view dashboards with real on‑chain numbers so you can verify claims yourself (very useful for learning with real data).
- Glassnode / Messari — readable charts and research with hard on‑chain and market numbers (Glassnode is especially good for plain charts and short commentary).
- Rekt (rekt.news / getrekt) and CertiK / DeFiLlama hack trackers — these publish post‑mortems and lists of real losses and exploits so you can learn from what actually went wrong.

Why this combo: Coin Bureau / Bankless give clear, beginner‑friendly explanations. Dune, Glassnode and Messari give verifiable numbers you can inspect. Rekt/CertiK/DeFiLlama show real losses and root causes (and often link to on‑chain evidence), which is the rare transparency you asked for.

If you want, I can:
- pick the single best beginner site for your specific interest (buying/holding, trading, DeFi, NFTs), or
- pull a short reading list + 3 Dune dashboards you can use to check real numbers yourself, or
- give links to the Rekt postmortems that teach the most common, avoidable mistakes.
